analyst_view.overall: Early view: Porto travel to the Azores six days after hosting Sporting and four days before Liverpool in the Champions League, so Farioli may rotate. Santa Clara are 4th with the joint second-best defence in the league (8 conceded) but have injuries to Guilherme Romão, Pedro Ferreira and Tiago Ferreira. The brief lists Emanuel Moreira and Pedro Pacheco as banned, but both bans fall on the Moreirense game on 28 November: Moreira's fifth-yellow ban is one match, and unless Pacheco's red card brings a longer ban (not yet published) both should be available here.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.3 goals. I lean slightly lower: these are the league's two best defences (Porto 5 conceded, Santa Clara 8), and Santa Clara like to keep the ball rather than chase games. Porto's priority between the Sporting and Liverpool games is likely to be a controlled win.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.8 corners. Santa Clara usually build patiently, as Petit described against Gil Vicente, and Porto will still have most of the territory. I see no reason to move the figure.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.7 cards. Santa Clara have had discipline problems lately (a red card and a fifth-yellow ban in the same week, and Petit complaining about refereeing), but the referee has not been named. I stay close to the site's figure.

shots.text: The numbers say 23.8 shots. With Porto possibly resting players before Liverpool, and Santa Clara's patient style, I lean a little lower. Their 27-5 goal record shows how little risk Porto take.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 7.1 shots on target, which already reflects two strong defences. If Santa Clara get their injured players back after the break they can keep the ball and limit Porto's chances. I keep to the site's figure.
